help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Health matters more than beauty; honesty more than punctuality.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The possibility is there, but the difficulty is time.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Adjectives ending in -ig take -keit, not -heit: die Traurigkeit.
help.tips[0].en.text: -heit after most adjectives: Freiheit, Gesundheit, Schönheit, Krankheit, Kindheit, Sicherheit. -keit after -ig / -lich / -bar / -sam: Möglichkeit, Freundlichkeit, Ehrlichkeit, Schwierigkeit, Pünktlichkeit, Dankbarkeit.
help.tips[0].en.title: -heit and -keit: always die
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The team's decision was a surprise.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The team has made an important decision.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Nouns in -ung are always feminine: die Rechnung.
help.tips[1].en.text: Verb → -ung: Entscheidung, Meinung, Erfahrung, Übung, Bedeutung, Wohnung, Zeitung, Rechnung. Noun → -schaft: Freundschaft, Wissenschaft, Gesellschaft, Mannschaft, Landschaft, Wirtschaft.
help.tips[1].en.title: -ung and -schaft: always die
help.tips[1].en.trap: these four suffixes never vary in gender. If you write 'der Meinung' as a nominative, the suffix has already told you you're wrong.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The intern and the scientist talked about tourism.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The artist and the student talked to the journalist.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Person nouns in -ant are masculine: der Praktikant (a woman is die Praktikantin).
help.tips[2].en.text: der Sportler, der Künstler, der Wissenschaftler, der Schüler · der Praktikant, der Lieferant, der Student, der Präsident (all n-Deklination) · der Journalist, der Tourist · der Tourismus, der Kapitalismus. Feminine: -lerin, -antin, -istin.
help.tips[2].en.title: People: -ler / -ner, -ant / -ent, -ist; -ismus
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: -tät joins -heit, -keit, -ung, -schaft and -ion in the feminine group: die Qualität.
help.tips[3].en.text: -heit, -keit, -ung, -schaft → die, every time. Add -ion (die Information) and -tät (die Universität) and you have the six most reliable gender rules in German.
help.tips[3].en.title: The die-quartet
help.context.en: My opinion on health: science gives us many possibilities, but the decision lies with each person. An athlete needs honesty with themselves, a good team needs friendship. And the greatest difficulty isn't the training but punctuality in the morning.
help.hookEn: Spot -heit, -keit, -ung or -schaft and you know the noun is feminine before you have even looked it up.
help.introEn: German builds abstract nouns with a handful of suffixes, each with a fixed gender — knowing them turns unknown words into known ones and gives you the article for free. Adjective + -heit → die: frei → die Freiheit, gesund → die Gesundheit, schön → die Schönheit. Adjective in -ig/-lich/-bar/-sam + -keit → die: möglich → die Möglichkeit, freundlich → die Freundlichkeit, ehrlich → die Ehrlichkeit. Verb + -ung → die: entscheiden → die Entscheidung, meinen → die Meinung, erfahren → die Erfahrung. Noun + -schaft → die: die Freundschaft, die Wissenschaft, die Gesellschaft. Persons: -ler / -ner → der: der Sportler, der Künstler, der Wissenschaftler; -ant / -ent → der (n-Deklination!): der Praktikant, der Student, der Lieferant; -ismus → der: der Tourismus, der Journalismus. Newspapers, forms and official letters are full of these, and reading them relies on you decoding them. In the quiz you form the noun from the word in brackets and, where the sentence has no article, write the article too — so the suffix gives you the gender as well as the word.
sentences[0].whyEn: Adjective + -heit = noun, always feminine: die Gesundheit.
sentences[1].whyEn: Verb + -ung: die Entscheidung — you 'meet' a decision in German.
sentences[5].whyEn: Noun + -schaft: die Freundschaft — the relationship as a noun.
sentences[6].whyEn: Wissen + -schaft: die Wissenschaft — in der Wissenschaft, dative.
sentences[9].whyEn: Sport + -ler: der Sportler — the person suffix -ler.
sentences[10].whyEn: der Praktikant — a weak noun, so accusative einen Praktikanten.
sentences[17].whyEn: ahnen + -ung: die Ahnung — keine Ahnung, 'no idea'!
